newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenians rally for third day against poll result.
newsitem.headline: Armenians rally for third day against poll result.

text.p: Thousands of Armenians rallied for a third day on Wednesday to protest against election results giving President Levon Ter-Petrosyan five more years in office and an opposition leader said the situation was "explosive".

Supporters of the president's main rival Vazgen Manukyan gathered near the national opera in central Yerevan as the election commission released results giving Ter-Petrosyan 52.09 percent of votes cast to 41.07 percent for his former prime minister.
They planned to march later in the day to parliament.

During a huge rally on Tuesday, troops took up positions inside the high fence surrounding the parliament building and more soldiers with riot shields and backed with water cannon surrounded Ter-Petrosyan's residence.

A leader of Manukyan's National Democratic Union (NDU) said on Wednesday Manukyan and his close aides were plotting their next move. They say they can prove that the vote was rigged and warn that their supporters might resort to violence.

"If the President, who directed the falsification of the election, insists on his fraudulent victory, then people will begin to choose dangerous methods. I am afraid this is unavoidable," said NDU parliamentarian Arshat Sadoyan.
The situation in the country was "explosive", he said.
Officials around Ter-Petrosyan, a former anti-Soviet dissident who has ruled this small Caucasus country of 3.5 million since independence in 1991, declined to comment on the allegations.
Most Armenians are still hurting from the economic collapse which followed the breakup of the Soviet Union and an eight-year war with neighbouring Azerbaijan over territory.

Ter-Petrosyan, an aloof 51-year-old academic, made few promises during the election campaign, focusing on stability, recent economic progress and victories over Azerbaijan while Manukyan pledged to revive industry and improve the people's lot.

Central Electoral Commission chairman Khachik Bezirjyan, who issued the final preliminary results on Wednesday, said official results would not be available for a few days. The turnout was 58.7 percent of the 2.2 million electorate.
Ter-Petrosyan needed a simple majority to avoid a second round runoff, but there were numerous incidences of obvious fraud committed by his supporters.

The electoral commission was meeting on Wednesday to discuss the allegations of irregularities. Bezirjyan faced angry questions from many of the 20 members of the commission, several of whom are NDU representatives.
The NDU, whose vote monitors watched counting, say they have certified copies of election protocols from nearly every one of the country's 1,742 polling places.
They say protocol totals indicate Manukyan won the election by 55 to 37 percent, but that regional electoral commissions changed many of them after they had been received from indvidual precincts.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which has been coordinating 89 interational observers, has issued a preliminary report criticising "very serious" irregularities in voting procedures.

The carefully-worded report did not question the overall legitimacy of the elections but stressed that its findings were preliminary and connected with the voting process itself rather than the counting process.
Individual observers saw a myriad of fraudulent and illegal activities being committed by Ter-Petrosyan forces.
